content:
maria: Quick check — finalizing per-route rate limit headers for /v2/generate. Plan: include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and an optional X-RateLimit-Burst when a route supports burst tokens. Want to lock format before docs publish. Any objections?

jason: Are we doing Reset in seconds (unix epoch) or milliseconds? Clients need clarity for Retry-After calculations.

maria: unix epoch seconds (consistent with other infra headers). We'll call it seconds to keep server/client math simple.

raj: For 429 responses: are we standardizing body shape? i.e., {"error": "rate_limited", "retry_after": 12} vs just relying on Retry-After header. Some clients use body.

sophie: SDKs currently read Retry-After header and fallback to parsing body.retry_after if present. We should keep both for backward compatibility.

maria: Agreed. Plan: return 429 with Retry-After header (seconds), X-RateLimit-Reset header, and body with `error: rate_limited` and `retry_after` in seconds. That keeps old clients working.

sam: What about soft-429s / degraded responses (we've discussed 'soft' token returns that are informative but not strict 429s)? How do headers behave there?

maria: For soft signals we'll use 200 + X-RateLimit-Soft: true and X-RateLimit-Remaining (may go negative) — but we want to avoid surprising clients. SDKs should treat X-RateLimit-Soft as advisory only.

raj: For per-route vs account-wide quotas — do we prefix headers with route id? e.g., X-Route-Limit or include X-RateLimit-Scope: route|account

maria: We'll include X-RateLimit-Scope: route|account plus X-RateLimit-Route: /v2/generate when scope=route. Keeps parsing simple.

jason: Quick nit: older client libs might choke on new headers. Should we document as non-breaking and add guidance to SDKs to ignore unknown headers.

sophie: SDK change already in progress to be resilient to unknown headers. We'll log and ignore unknowns. No version bump required.

api-bot: deploybot: canary rollout of header changes started at canary-01. Watch logs in #eng-runtime.

maria: Example headers we plan to document:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 95
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000123   # unix epoch seconds
X-RateLimit-Scope: route
X-RateLimit-Route: /v2/generate
X-RateLimit-Burst: 20   # optional, present only for burstable routes
```

And 429 example:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000135
Content-Type: application/json

{"error": "rate_limited", "retry_after": 12}
```

sam: Should we add an X-RateLimit-Bucket header for client debugging (like per-customer bucket id)? Could help support.

maria: +1. We'll add X-RateLimit-Bucket (string) in canary and make it optional. Not required for SDKs.

raj: One more: TTL semantics for Reset — is Reset absolute epoch or seconds until reset? You said epoch. Confirm.

maria: Confirmed: absolute unix epoch seconds. If we need 'seconds until reset' later we can add X-RateLimit-Reset-Delta but prefer single canonical field now.

jason: Docs task? I'll add a short PR to the api-spec repo with header glossary and example snippets.

sophie: I'll tweak SDK parsing to handle X-RateLimit-Soft and X-RateLimit-Burst gracefully.

maria: OK — actionables: jason docs PR, sophie SDK changes, runtime will emit X-RateLimit-Bucket and Scope on canary. If no major issues by EOD we'll promote. Thanks :thumbsup:

sam: LGTM

maria: marking this resolved for now — ping if you see anything in canary logs.
